newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: IMF delays Yugo membership decision to June 1997.
newsitem.headline: IMF delays Yugo membership decision to June 1997.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has once again postponed a decision on Yugoslavia's status in the Fund, the Tanjug news agency reported on Tuesday.
This is the eighth time the IMF postponed its decision on Yugoslavia's membership. The first such decision was made on June 14, 1993.
The Yugoslav Finance Minister Tomica Raicevic told Tanjug of the postponement, but did not give any further details.

"Yugoslavia has managed to harmonize key legal documents needed to normalise relations with the IMF and to reach a principle agreement on payment of matured liabilities," Tanjug quoted Raicevic as saying.
Since there is very little time left to solve those issues, the IMF Board of Governors decided to postpone until June 14, 1997, its decision on Yugoslavia's status in the Fund, the minister said.
Raicevic said he expected Yugoslavia would normalize its relations with the IMF and other financial institutions over next six months.

Sanctions were lifted earlier this year, and Yugoslavia has been trying to send a clear message to the IMF that there are no barriers, either political or economic, that would stop it from meeting obligations as a fund member.
No one at the finance ministry was immediately available for comment. -- Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
